Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time ceased operations, one of its co-founders, Antonio Pinto, immediately announced the launch of a brand new TV and film tracking app called Bingers, which focuses on richer social features. Details are as follows.

Bingers is now available for download

Whip Media previously announced it would shut down the TV tracking app TV Time, and one of the app's co-founders promptly announced the launch of Bingers, positioning it as a "watchlist with speed, beauty, and fun community features."

According to TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android platforms. For users still looking for an alternative to TV Time, this app can be considered a spiritual successor to the now-defunct platform—TV Time was once one of the most popular TV tracking apps globally.

Users who previously used TV Time and backed up their data through the export tool can import their database into Bingers, seamlessly connecting with their original viewing records; users who never exported their data, or new users who have never used a TV tracking app before, can start building their watchlist from scratch.

Bingers places great emphasis on community-driven features, including personal profiles, rating and commenting on shows, GIF stickers, polls, and character popularity votes, among others. Pinto told TechCrunch that these are precisely the features that made TV Time so popular over the years:

If users simply want to track the TV dramas and movies they have watched, Bingers offers dedicated watchlist and viewing history features. Similar to TV Time, the platform also displays a calendar of upcoming episodes and premieres, along with a countdown feature showing how many days remain until broadcast.

Bingers is available for free download on the App Store, and currently does not offer in-app purchases.
